title: Relationship types the codebase-memory-mcp edges need
rationale: Phase 2 maps every codebase-memory-mcp (CBM) edge the relationship catalog can hold (spec/analyzers/cbm/edge-mapping.json). These CBM edges have no catalog triple to land on: INHERITS, OVERRIDE, EMITS, ASYNC_CALLS, RAISES, LISTENS_ON (interface level), CONTAINS_FOLDER, HTTP_CALLS (and the gRPC, GraphQL and tRPC variants) and CONNECTS_TO. Each addition below is a new meaning between its pair, checked against the catalog so that none restates an existing relationship in the other direction (design charter: one meaning, one predicate). The inventory's addition 6 (component uses application service) was dropped for that reason: application.applicationservice serves application.applicationcomponent already says it. Additions 8 and 10 were dropped because the existing reversed triples (technology.systemsoftware serves application.applicationcomponent; technology.node composes technology.artifact) express SPAWNS and DEPLOYS. Source: docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, 'Catalog additions the edge mapping would need'.

additions.description: An application component is a specialised kind of another component: it inherits the general component's structure and behaviour and refines part of it, and can stand wherever the general one is expected.
evidence: A class extending another class of the same codebase where both are modelled as components (class FileStore extends BaseStore, class Owner(Person) with behaviour), recorded by CBM as an INHERITS edge.

additions.observed: INHERITS between interfaces and data classes (counts included above)
additions.description: A data object is a subtype of another data object: it carries every field of the general one and adds or narrows some, so an instance of it is also an instance of the general one.
evidence: A TypeScript interface or type extending another (interface ImportResult extends BaseResult), or a data class deriving from another data class, both classified as application data objects; CBM INHERITS.

additions.description: An application function refines another function's behaviour for a more specific case: it overrides the general function and is used in its place for that case.
evidence: A method marked @Override, or a subclass method with the same name and signature as its parent's, both modelled as functions; CBM OVERRIDE.

additions.observed: EMITS and ASYNC_CALLS documented by CBM, not observed in the eval corpora; RAISES 75 / 0 / 0
additions.description: An application function raises or publishes an application event when it runs; the event exists because the function emitted it.
evidence: emit('order-placed'), eventBus.publish(...), producer.send(topic, ...) or raising a domain event inside a function body; CBM EMITS to a Channel, or ASYNC_CALLS to a queue or topic route.

additions.description: An application component publishes an application event on a channel, queue or topic as part of its behaviour, without one function of it being modelled as the publisher.
evidence: A class or module that owns a message producer or socket emitter for a named channel, queue or topic, where the emitting functions are below element granularity; CBM EMITS or ASYNC_CALLS from the file.

additions.description: An application interface is an entry point that listens for an application event: it does its work when the event arrives and cannot work without it.
evidence: A message-listener class or handler entry point such as @KafkaListener, @EventListener, @RabbitListener, a socket.io on('event') handler set or a webhook receiver, modelled as an application interface; CBM LISTENS_ON.

additions.description: An application component is made up of sub-components that exist only as its parts, such as a package or directory-level component and the modules inside it.
evidence: A directory or package modelled as a component (src/analyzers/, a Java package, a Python package with __init__.py) containing modules or subpackages modelled as components; CBM CONTAINS_FOLDER and CONTAINS_FILE.

additions.observed: HTTP_CALLS between corpus symbols and routes (fastapi frontend client calls)
additions.description: An application function calls an API operation as a client: it consumes the operation's functionality over the network.
evidence: fetch('/api/v1/items'), axios.post(...), a generated SDK call (ItemsService.createItem) or a gRPC or GraphQL client call inside a function, resolved by CBM to the operation's route; CBM HTTP_CALLS, GRPC_CALLS, GRAPHQL_CALLS or TRPC_CALLS.

additions.description: An application component is a client of an API operation: code inside it calls the operation, and the calling functions are below element granularity.
evidence: An API client class or module (a generated SDK service, a backend-for-frontend adapter) whose methods call the operation's route; CBM HTTP_CALLS from the component's file.

additions.observed: CONNECTS_TO documented by CBM, not observed (needs the infrastructure pass)
additions.description: A node (a workload or compose service) depends on a technology service it connects to; it cannot run correctly when that service is unavailable. This is the consumer side, distinct from technology.technologyservice depends-on technology.node, where the service depends on the node that hosts it.
evidence: A Kubernetes Deployment or docker-compose service whose environment, config or code addresses another Service by name (DATABASE_URL=postgres://db:5432, http://payments-svc); CBM CONNECTS_TO.
additions.reverse_differs: technology.technologyservice depends-on technology.node is the hosting dependency (a service needs the node it runs on); this is the consumer dependency (a workload needs a service it calls). depends-on is directional, so the two are different meanings.

additions.observed: infrastructure DEPENDS_ON (docker-compose depends_on between services); needs the infrastructure pass
additions.description: A node depends on another node to run: it is started after it and fails without it, as a compose service declares depends_on another service.
evidence: A docker-compose service with depends_on: [db], or an init container or startup probe that waits for another workload, each side modelled as a technology node; CBM DEPENDS_ON between infrastructure nodes.
